item.title: Ohio State Defeats Minnesota, 60-55, in Big Ten Tournament Quarterfinals
item.description: Ohio State avenged its regular-season loss to Minnesota in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals. Just over two weeks after losing their only regular-season matchup with Minnesota, the fifth-seeded Buckeyes punched their ticket to the Big Ten Tournament semifinals with a 60-55 win over the No. 4 seed Gophers in Indianapolis. item.title: Ohio State Can Clinch Double-Bye in Big Ten Tournament With Win Over Indiana
item.description: There are many reasons to lock into Ohio State's game against Indiana on Saturday. The Buckeyes can all but secure their first NCAA Tournament berth in four years. Bruce Thornton is 12 points away from breaking the school's all-time scoring record on Senior Night. It's also his bobblehead night. But there are also direct implications for the Big Ten Tournament. item.title: Remember When: Dennis Hopson Scores 32 Points in Ohio State's Win Over Kentucky in the First Round of the 1987 NCAA Tournament
item.description: A day after former Ohio State coach Woody Hayes passed away, Dennis Hopson did what he did best: Score plenty of points while leading the Buckeyes to a win. With Ohio State holding a 20-12 record and donning black shoulder patches in remembrance of Hayes, the No. 9-seeded Buckeyes were set to play No. 8 seed Kentucky in the first round of the 1987 NCAA Tournament, a team OSU was a perfect 4-0 against in the tournament. item.title: Ohio State Falls to No. 1 Seed UCLA, 72-62, in Big Ten Tournament Semifinals
item.description: Ohio State’s Big Ten Tournament run ended with a semifinal loss to UCLA for the second year in a row. After beating Indiana and Minnesota in their first two games of Big Ten Tournament play, the Buckeyes (26-7) were unable to dethrone the conference’s top team on Saturday, falling 72-62 to No. 1 seed UCLA (30-1) in the semifinals. item.title: Press Coverage: Bruce Thornton Makes History in Fitting Fashion As Ohio State Positions Itself to Make First NCAA Tournament in Four Years
item.description: It was a historic and drought-ending night for Ohio State men’s basketball in the Buckeyes’ regular-season finale. In front of a sellout crowd at the Schottenstein Center, Bruce Thornton became Ohio State’s all-time leading scorer, breaking Dennis Hopson’s all-time record of 2,096 points with a 3-pointer late in the first half. item.title: Ohio State Earns No. 8 Seed, Double-Bye in Big Ten Tournament
item.description: Ohio State's Big Ten Tournament position is set. With Ohio State beating Indiana and UCLA beating USC on Saturday night, the Buckeyes are locked in as the No. 8 seed heading into the conference tourney. They beat out Iowa by one game for the final double-bye spot. Ohio State will play its first game of the Big Ten Tournament on Thursday, facing the winner of the ninth-seeded Hawkeyes and the winner of the No. 16 vs. No. 17 seed game between Oregon and Maryland.
